values.value: • Use the strength of the relationship to get honest guidance on the path to close. • Validate that both influencer and decision maker are aligned, not just personally positive. • Ask what could still derail the deal internally. • Use the trust to secure a dated next step and clearer buying process. • Keep the relationship active through closure, not just discovery.
10|Yes
Buyer may say, 'We are aligned, just give us time.' Response: 'Of course. To help the process, what is the next internal step and who should be involved from here?'
Good. Use that access to test truth early and move the decision maker closer to the business case, not just the demo.
Low risk. Keep decision-maker access active.
Ask: 'What would you need to see or hear to feel confident taking this forward internally?'
Yes

• Strengthen weak links rather than assuming one sponsor is enough. • Map who likes you, who knows you, and who still needs to be won over. • Build separate value narratives for influencer and decision maker. • Ask your current contact to help expand access in a natural way. • Do not progress as if full buyer coverage already exists.
10|Partially
Buyer may say, 'You can work through me for now.' Response: 'Happy to. At the same time, it would help if I can also align with the people who will shape the final decision.'
Strengthen direct access. One good champion is helpful, but it is not enough if the final buyer is distant.
Risk: Partial access creates last-minute surprises.
Ask: 'Would it make sense to include the final approver in the next discussion so we can align early?'
Partially

• Reduce dependence on the intermediary wherever possible. • Respect the channel or introducer, but build direct credibility with the buyer. • Ask for a joint meeting so you can hear needs first-hand. • Avoid sending major proposal revisions through a single go-between. • Direct access will improve win rate and reduce distortion.
10|Through 3rd party
Buyer may say, 'Please route everything through our consultant/partner.' Response: 'Certainly. It would still help to have one direct conversation as well so I can align accurately and avoid rework.'
Do not stay dependent on an intermediary. Win a direct conversation with the buyer or you will lose control.
High risk: You are selling through a filter.
Say: 'To make this useful, I would value 20 minutes with the main decision maker as well.'
Through 3rd party

• This is a serious weakness. Do not pretend the deal is controlled. • Get access to the buyer side intentionally through a relevant conversation, not a random introduction ask. • Lead with insight or value that earns a meeting. • Find a warm route in through existing customers, partners, or internal references if possible. • Until buyer access improves, avoid late-stage behaviour like discounting or proposal chasing.
10|No

Buyer may say, 'It is difficult to get the decision maker involved now.' Response: 'Understood. Even one short alignment call at the right time can prevent delays and help us tailor this much better.'
Do not progress to proposal without buyer access. First earn a meeting with the decision maker and key influencer.
High risk: No access to authority.
Ask: 'Who besides your team should join the next call so the decision can move faster?'
No
Do we have a good relationship with the decision maker and the influencer?
